headline: Highest risk is medium: EMQX’s broad network egress can carry IoT data, but LightZero has no filesystem, network, or MCP surfaces to create a stronger pairwise pathway.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No plausible prompt-injection bridge is documented. EMQX exposes only an HTTP API and broad network egress, while LightZero has no read/write filesystem, MCP, browser, or subprocess surfaces to ingest attacker-controlled instructions by default.
conditions: IF LightZero is wrapped with a manual copy-paste workflow from EMQX outputs, then prompt injection becomes possible.
mitigations: Keep the agents disconnected from shared clipboard or chat channels.
Do not paste EMQX output into LightZero prompts.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging if a shared message bus is introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: EMQX touches IoT data and has broad network egress, but LightZero has no filesystem read/write or network egress, so the pair lacks a documented path for LightZero to exfiltrate shared data. The main risk is limited to unusual operator-mediated transfer.
conditions: IF an operator copies IoT data from EMQX into LightZero inputs, then that data can be exposed in LightZero logs or outputs.
mitigations: Avoid placing IoT data into LightZero prompts or files.
Use synthetic or redacted samples for any LightZero testing.
Keep EMQX and LightZero on separate accounts or workspaces.
requires-engineering: add DLP controls on any manual export path.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: No overlapping write or mutable-resource capabilities are present. EMQX has broad network egress and HTTP API access, while LightZero explicitly lacks filesystem write, git modification, shell, subprocess, and network egress, so there is no shared write surface to conflict over.
conditions: IF LightZero is later granted filesystem or git write access to the same directory as EMQX, then write conflicts could emerge.
mitigations: Do not mount a shared writable workspace.
requires-engineering: add locking if shared mutable state is introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A cascading-error pathway is weak because LightZero is a game-playing agent with no documented action-taking authority, and EMQX is an IoT broker/scheduler with HTTP API exposure rather than a fact-producing planner. Any harmful chain would require an operator to treat EMQX output as authoritative and feed it into LightZero manually.
conditions: IF an operator uses EMQX output as authoritative input to LightZero without verification, then downstream errors can propagate.
mitigations: Do not automate LightZero actions from EMQX text.
Keep a human review step between the agents.
requires-engineering: add schema validation for any handoff.

E_compliance.rationale: Compliance risk is limited and one-sided: EMQX touches IoT data, but LightZero lists no data classes touched and no residency or retention constraints. There is no documented cross-border or regulated-data transfer path between them, so only narrow policy mismatch risk remains.
conditions: IF regulated IoT data is exported from EMQX into LightZero artifacts, then retention or residency policy mismatches may apply.
mitigations: Do not export regulated IoT data into LightZero.
Confirm retention settings on any shared storage.
requires-engineering: document a data-handling policy for cross-tool transfers.
